form-label-and-group-relationships-by-co.mechanism: Every input is correctly labelled: each <label> has a real for= pointing at a real input id with a descriptive name ('Number of guests'->#guests, 'Preferred date'->#visit-date, 'Mobile number'->#mobile, 'Party name'->#party-name), so axe/WAVE/Lighthouse pass. The defect is a visual/programmatic mismatch: the labels and inputs are separate CSS-grid items whose grid-row/grid-column placement paints each label directly above an input it is NOT wired to (the inputs are swapped within each row). A sighted user types into the box captioned 'Preferred date' but its programmatic label is 'Number of guests'; a screen-reader user, following the for/id graph, gets the opposite pairing. The visible label-to-field relationship contradicts the programmatic one.
form-label-and-group-relationships-by-co.scenario: E-commerce/booking 'Reserve a tasting' form whose four text inputs are correctly associated via <label for>/id, but a 2-column CSS grid repaints the input cells swapped within each row so each visible caption sits above a different field than its programmatic label (e.g. 'Preferred date' label over the #guests input). The label-to-field relationship is only correct programmatically, contradicting the visual layout.
